evidence: src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts lend(): `const loan = await this.lending.lend(...); await this.history.note(loan.id, 'lent');` — the controller decides that lending must produce a history record (a domain/business workflow rule)

src/presentation/http/LoanController.ts giveBack(): `const fine = await this.lending.giveBack(body.loanId, new Date()); await this.history.note(body.loanId, 'returned');` — the same business sequencing for returns happens in the presentation layer
Everything else in the file is presentation work: request DTOs, renderLoan(loan), and HttpResult status codes 201/200
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of LoanController is ordinary presentation work. It defines the request DTOs (LendRequest, ReturnRequest), takes data from the request body, calls business services, renders through LoanView and builds HttpResult status codes. One responsibility belongs in the domain layer, though. The controller decides that every lend and every return must be recorded in the loan history. It does this by calling LoanHistoryService.note right after LendingService.lend and LendingService.giveBack. That pairing is a business workflow rule: if a loan changes state, a history event is recorded. Because the rule lives in the HTTP adapter, any other entry point that calls LendingService skips it, and the two calls don't run as a single business operation. LendingService, or an application service in the business layer, should own this sequencing. The controller should make one call. The historyOf handler and the `new Date()` clock argument are acceptable at this edge. This is a judgment call, since this kind of orchestration is sometimes tolerated in thin controllers, so confidence is moderate.

violations.message: lend() and giveBack() combine LendingService state changes with LoanHistoryService.note(...) calls. They hold the business rule 'every lend and every return is recorded in loan history', which belongs in the business (domain) layer, for example inside LendingService or an application service. It shouldn't live in the HTTP controller.
